chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ubaydillah ibn Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him), from Jafar al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), narrated to me from Ubaydillah ibn Nahik, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hanifah al-Sabiq [al-Sa'iq], from Yunus ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
If you are close to him – referring to al-Husayn (peace be upon him) – and you are able to perform Ghusl, then perform it; otherwise, perform Wudu and then go to him.

key_terms.الْحُسَيْنَ: Imam al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), the third Imam.
key_terms.تَوَضَّأْ: Perform minor ablution (Wudu), a ritual washing of specific body parts.
key_terms.غُسْلًا: Ritual bath (Ghusl), a major ablution required for ritual purity.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing Ghusl versus Wudu before visiting Imam Husayn's shrine?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes a pragmatic legal hierarchy for ritual purity, prioritizing accessibility to ensure the spiritual connection with Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) is not hindered by strict ritual requirements. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *ease* (*yusr*) in worship, allowing Wudu as a valid substitute for Ghusl when water or time is limited, thereby encouraging consistent visitation regardless of one's physical circumstances.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 4. Ja’far ibn Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn ‘Ubaydillāh ibn Mūsā Al-Kāżim (a.s.) ibn Jafar Al-Sādiq (a.s.), narrated to me from ‘Ubaydillāh ibn Nahīk, from Muḥammad ibn Ziyād, from Abī Ḥanīfah Al-Sābiq, from Yūnus ibn ‘Ammār, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:
If you are close (in proximity) to him – referring to Ḥusain (a.s.) – and it is possible to perform Ghusl before going to him, do so. Otherwise, perform Wuďū and then go to him.
